claim.pdf_says: 8.3.3.2.4   General rules  (a fifth-level clause under 8.3.3.2 Alphanumeric literals, sibling of 8.3.3.2.1 General, 8.3.3.2.2 General format, 8.3.3.2.3 Syntax rules)
claim.why_it_matters: The heading is emitted at level 2 while its parent 8.3.3.2 is level 3 (`### 8.3.3.2 Alphanumeric literals`) and its own siblings 8.3.3.2.1/.2/.3 are level 4 (`#### ...`). The child therefore outranks its parent in the document outline: any generated table of contents or heading-based navigation places 8.3.3.2.4 General rules outside 8.3.3.2, detaching the alphanumeric-literal general rules from the clause they belong to.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) Nothing is missing. The claim is filed as kind=missing-heading, but the heading is present verbatim and correctly placed. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:5896-5897 reads `` / `## 8.3.3.2.4 General rules`, sitting exactly where the PDF puts it: after syntax rule 6) ("Each hex-character-sequence-1 shall consist of ...") and before "ALL FORMATS" / general rule 1). Number, title, anchor slug and position all match the rendered page. Zero characters of content are absent. The claim itself quotes the markdown containing the heading it calls missing, so it is self-refuting as filed. (2) The PDF contains no heading-level information for the markdown to have gotten wrong. I rendered pages 137 and 138 at 300 dpi and read the printed glyphs. On p137 the headings `8.3.3.2 Alphanumeric literals`, `8.3.3.2.1 General`, `8.3.3.2.2 General format` and `8.3.3.2.3 Syntax rules` are set in the SAME bold face, at the SAME point size, at the SAME left margin, with the same tab gap between number and title. On p138 `8.3.3.2.4 General rules` is typographically IDENTICAL to all four. ISO makes no visual distinction whatsoever between the parent clause 8.3.3.2 and its four subclauses in this range - depth is carried solely by the dotted decimal number. The markdown transcribes that number exactly ("8.3.3.2.4"), i.e. it preserves 100% of the hierarchy the PDF actually encodes. The `###` vs `####` levels the claim treats as ground truth are themselves inventions of the transcription pipeline, not readings of the source; there is no PDF fact in conflict. (3) The stated harm is factually false on its own terms. A `## Page 138` marker (level 2) is emitted at line 5880, i.e. BETWEEN `#### 8.3.3.2.3 Syntax rules` (line 5865) and `## 8.3.3.2.4 General rules` (line 5897). In any heading-based outline that level-2 page marker already closes the 8.3.3.2 subtree before 8.3.3.2.4 is reached. Re-tagging 8.3.3.2.4 as `####` would therefore NOT nest it under 8.3.3.2 - it would nest it under `## Page 138`. The alleged defect does not cause the claimed detachment, and the proposed correction would not cure it. The detachment is produced entirely by the page-marker furniture, which the verification brief explicitly names as non-defect. (4) It is systemic formatting, not a page-138 content discrepancy. Heading depth restarts per page slice throughout the file: the first clause heading after every page break is promoted to `##` regardless of its true depth. In the immediate neighbourhood alone: `## 8.3.3.3` (first on p139), `## 8.3.3.4` (first on p140), `## 8.3.3.4.4` and `## 8.3.3.5` (p141), `## 8.3.3.5.3` (p142), `## 8.3.3.6.2` (p144), `## 8.3.3.6.3` (p144) - each with deeper-numbered children correctly at `###`/`####` below it. The file carries 1,261 `## Page NNN` markers and 947 `# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)` running-header level-1s interleaved with clause headings, and the pipeline even promotes plain body labels to headings (`## FORMAT 1` through `## FORMAT 4` on p146). The markdown heading tree is comprehensively non-semantic by construction; singling out 8.3.3.2.4 as a page-138 discrepancy misattributes a document-wide rendering convention to a transcription error on this page. Meaning is unchanged: any consumer resolving a citation to "8.3.3.2.4" - the spec's own canonical hierarchy device, transcribed exactly - lands on the correct, complete text. This is formatting, not content. Collateral check performed while on the page: the p138 opening continuation fragment "...normally recognized by that implementation; the implementor shall specify any applicable syntax rules." is NOT lost - it is present at line 5877, correctly rejoined to the paragraph it continues from p137. Body text on this page reconciles cleanly.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading 8.3.3.2.4 General rules is present, correctly numbered, correctly anchored and correctly positioned; no text is missing. The finding is really about the markdown heading LEVEL, which (a) transcribes nothing from the PDF - ISO sets 8.3.3.2 and all of 8.3.3.2.1/.2/.3/.4 in identical bold at identical size, encoding depth only in the dotted number, which the markdown reproduces exactly; (b) does not produce the claimed harm, because a level-2 `## Page 138` marker between 8.3.3.2.3 and 8.3.3.2.4 already breaks the outline irrespective of this heading's level; and (c) is a document-wide pipeline convention in which the first clause heading after any page break is promoted to `##` (same pattern at 8.3.3.3, 8.3.3.4, 8.3.3.4.4, 8.3.3.5, 8.3.3.5.3, 8.3.3.6.2, 8.3.3.6.3, and even on non-headings such as `## FORMAT 1`). If the outline is ever wanted as a navigable tree, that is a single global post-processing change to the transcription pipeline - normalize clause-heading depth from the dotted number and demote page/running-header furniture below all clause headings - not a per-page content fix, and not a defect to ledger against page 138.
